title: The Art of War

sections.title: Why jumping into critical tasks without verified skill leads
sections.narration: You trust untested people to handle your important projects. Years ago, researchers discovered that putting inexperienced workers in charge creates massive disasters. Industrial psychologist Frank Schmidt studied this exact issue in 1998. The result? Total breakdown. Unskilled workers make about three times more costly errors on complex tasks than trained staff. Management professor Robert Kaplan also tracked strategic failure in 2005. He found that about 70 percent of corporate strategic initiatives fail due to poor execution. Assigning critical duties to unproven people almost guarantees a complete mess. Sun Tzu warned against this exact mistake thousands of years ago. "The ancients were particularly chary of allowing mere novices to botch their work." They knew that enthusiasm never replaces proven competence. When you hand vital tasks to untried hands, you invite personal failure. Real skill requires actual testing before the battle begins.

sections.narration: You might think fame naturally proves a person's real ability. But famous names often get false credit for work they never did.
